summary: Re-run of iter79 Plan C4/C5/C6/C7 (workout editor + regenerate) after E1 fixes. ALL 30/30 iter79 tests now PASS (previously 21/30). E1's fix suite validated end-to-end: (1) server._log_change signature widened to accept optional kind + at kwargs — all 7 feature_coach_workout_editor callsites work; (2) _log_change dual-writes to BOTH db.coach_change_log (legacy) AND db.change_log (unified) with try/except on each write; (3) coach_programme_regenerate_apply inserts gen_job FIRST and wraps _log_change in try/except so a log failure can never cause a phantom 500 → double-enqueue. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iter80_log_change_dualwrite.py (4 supplementary tests, all PASS): S1 verifies PATCH /coach/workouts/{wid} writes a workout+kind=edit entry to BOTH collections with correct meta.workout_id; S2 confirms /api/coach/clients/{cid}/programme-timeline surfaces the workout-edit event (reads from db.change_log); S3a in-process monkey-patches db.change_log.insert_one to raise and confirms _log_change swallows the failure (legacy write still succeeds); S3b confirms POST /programme/regenerate-apply returns 200 and creates exactly 1 gen_jobs row. Regression: Plan A (iter75), Plan B (iter76), Plan D (iter77) and Plan C1-C3 (iter78) suites all green. Combined run: 110/110 PASS (one initial flake was a network timeout to the preview URL; test passed clean on retry). No new deprecated-package or React Native red-screen issues detected. Frontend not re-tested this iteration — E1's changes are backend-only and prior iter79 F1/F2/F3 smoke was green.

minor.issue: dual-write is intentional per E1 fix. Once all consumers migrate to db.change_log, db.coach_change_log can be sunset. No action required now.

action_items: None — all fixes verified. Safe to move on.

OPTIONAL follow-up (from prior iter79 minor list, still open): reconsider whether db.coach_change_log should be sunset in favour of the unified db.change_log stream after a migration window; both are being written today.
OPTIONAL follow-up: V2 search .to_list(limit) argument should be the post-clamp value rather than raw limit (cosmetic, no user impact).
critical_code_review_comments: server._log_change now correctly wraps each collection write in try/except with logger.exception — a Mongo hiccup on either write can never break a caller. Well done.

feature_coach_workout_editor.coach_programme_regenerate_apply now inserts gen_job FIRST and wraps _log_change in try/except — the previously observed 'phantom 500 → double-enqueue' vector is closed. Verified via S3b: single POST → 200 + exactly one gen_jobs row.
kind and at kwargs are optional on _log_change with sensible defaults (at defaults to now_iso() via `ts = at or now_iso()`) — clean, backwards-compatible extension.

Both writes assign a fresh new_id() so Motor's autogenerated _id on the same dict does not collide between collections (line 8178). This is the correct pattern; consider a code comment referencing why.

Callers should be reminded that _log_change is now truly best-effort — any callsite that relies on the log entry being present for correctness (unlikely) would need to check independently. Current callers only use it for audit UX which is the intended contract.

success_rate.backend: 110/110 = 100% (Plan A 21 + Plan B 26 + Plan D 20 + Plan C1-C3 15 + Plan C4-C7 30 + Iter80 supplementary 4). One test flaked once on a network ConnectTimeout to the preview URL — passed clean on immediate retry.
success_rate.frontend: not re-tested this iteration — backend-only fixes; iter79 F1/F2/F3 smoke was green

Motor is bound to the first-imported test module's event loop (established pattern from iter77+). Preview URL is occasionally flaky on long test batches — a single ConnectTimeout on a POST is not a real regression; re-run the specific class to confirm.

All 9 previously-failing tests are now green because: (a) server._log_change signature accepts `kind` and `at` kwargs, (b) the helper dual-writes to both change-log collections with per-write try/except, (c) coach_programme_regenerate_apply orders gen_job insert BEFORE the log call and wraps the log call in try/except.
